ehlers2024.title: Data Assimilation and Parameter Identification for Water Waves Using the Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation and Physics-Informed Neural Networks
ehlers2024.access_level: Published primary record and publisher/institutional full text inspected; author manuscript at https://arxiv.org/html/2401.03708v1 also inspected. Institutional published PDF: https://tore.tuhh.de/dspace-cris-server/api/core/bitstreams/d014f972-c436-476d-861a-737bc0434adc/content .
evidence: Hydrodynamic NLS PINN reconstruction on 630 synthetic HOS wave-tank samples; observations at x=3 and 6 m, withheld test gauges at x=4 and 5 m.
Learning carrier frequency/wavenumber alongside the field reduced reported mean SSP from 0.204 to 0.186, reported as an 8.82 percent improvement.
limitations: Synthetic measurements; no laboratory experiment in this paper. Broader spectra and higher steepness remained difficult.
Effective coefficient fitting does not itself establish physical parameter identifiability or a correct nonlinear dispersion relation.
No independent reproduction was performed in this literature review.
explicit_future_work: Published Conclusions explicitly suggest Dysthe/MNLSE residuals and the broader-bandwidth MNLSE.
Other stated directions include varying gauge separation, deriving a nonlinear dispersion relation from fitted parameters, and using real wave measurements.
Fully nonlinear potential-flow PINNs are also proposed, but subsequent 2025 work has already pursued that direction.

ehlers2025.title: Physics-informed neural networks for phase-resolved data assimilation and prediction of nonlinear ocean waves
ehlers2025.access_level: APS publisher metadata/abstract inspected; detailed method/results/outlook inspected in the full author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2501.08430v1 . Publisher full article requires access.
evidence: Two coupled potential-flow PINNs represent free-surface elevation and velocity potential, with Fourier features, hard measurement constraints and ReLoBRaLo loss balancing.
Author manuscript reports laboratory flume reconstruction SSP=0.049, and an example forecasting approximately one peak period beyond four observed snapshots.
limitations: This is potential-flow work, not a Dysthe PINN implementation.
Forecast accuracy declines beyond the assimilation interval; inferred laboratory velocity potential lacks independently measured ground truth.
The manuscript HTML's generated August 2026 header is not the journal publication date.
explicit_future_work: Faster training, multi-GPU optimization, pretraining with fine-tuning, and physics-informed neural operators.
Directional wave fields, variable bathymetry and related engineering applications. Directional/bathymetric extensions are outside the approved project baseline.
The generic PINO suggestion is already pursued by the subsequent wavepino paper.

wavepino.title: Bridging ocean wave physics and deep learning: Physics-informed neural operators for nonlinear wavefield reconstruction in real-time
wavepino.access_level: Publisher metadata and abstract inspected at https://pubs.aip.org/aip/pof/article/37/10/107119/3366763/Bridging-ocean-wave-physics-and-deep-learning ; detailed results and outlook inspected in full author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2508.03315v1 . Public author repository inspected; not executed.
evidence: FNO-based PINO constrained by potential-flow free-surface boundary conditions; synthetic HOS data, split into 634 training, 211 validation and 211 test cases.
Five buoy time series or radar snapshots plus one calibration buoy; author manuscript reports mean SSP 0.1035 and 0.1341, respectively.
A representative reconstructed sample takes 0.014 seconds after training; this is inference latency, not total cost.
limitations: Demonstrated on synthetic long-crested unidirectional wave fields, not deployed multidirectional ocean observations.
PINO constraints are potential flow, not the approved spatial Dysthe equation. Generic sparse-wave PINO reconstruction is therefore already occupied novelty.
Detailed manuscript numbers were not independently reproduced.
explicit_future_work: Extension to multidirectional 2D+t fields, with increased computational requirements and possible parallelization.

hosdata.title: Data to train a physics-informed neural operator for ocean wave reconstruction
hosdata.access_level: Public author-deposited primary dataset record inspected; 3.2 GB file not downloaded or validated.
evidence: Public dataset_1056_samples_HOS_ele_pot_inte.npz, approximately 3.2 GB, linked to DOI 10.1063/5.0294655 and the author code repository.
limitations: HOS provenance must be preserved; these arrays are not Dysthe solutions.
Using a subset for Dysthe validation requires a documented elevation-to-envelope observation map and a justified physical-validity filter.
The dataset record's related-journal year does not supersede the publisher's verified 2025 article date.

extreme2026.title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
extreme2026.access_level: Primary arXiv metadata and abstract inspected; not full-text reviewed or independently reproduced. Author spelling retained as listed in that primary record.
evidence: Two-stage learned dynamics and physics-informed neural search; abstract describes Duffing/homoclinic, stationary NLS/Townes and Liouville examples.
limitations: Recent preprint; not evidence of a validated Dysthe predictor or sparse water-wave reconstruction method.
Rogue waves and singularities are prospective applications, not demonstrated Dysthe results in the inspected abstract.
explicit_future_work: Abstract proposes other coherent structures, including rogue waves, compactons, peakons and potentially singularities.

fedele.title: Hamiltonian description and traveling waves of the spatial Dysthe equations
fedele.venue: arXiv:1110.3605v3, research report; first submitted 17 October 2011
fedele.access_level: Primary arXiv record verified; current local model contract and corresponding solver source inspected for the adopted equation convention.
evidence: Gauge transformation reveals a Hamiltonian formulation and invariants for spatial Dysthe equations; numerical traveling waves and inelastic collisions are studied.
Local approved free-surface contract cites equation (1.3), coefficient tuple (a,h,c,e,f)=(1,1,8,2,2), with a nonlocal |D_tau| mean-flow derivative.
limitations: This source is not a PINN study. Its numerical traveling waves do not establish nonlinear stability or integrability.
The free-surface envelope is noncanonical; generic NLS Hamiltonian constraints require careful transformation and boundary conventions.
The metadata here describes this exact arXiv research report, not an assumed journal publication under a similar title.
